newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Moslems protest arrest of Shi'ite leader.
newsitem.headline: Indian Moslems protest arrest of Shi'ite leader.

text.p: Police used water cannon in the Indian capital on Friday to disperse some 500 Moslem demonstrators protesting against the arrest of a Shi'ite leader who campaigned to end a 20-year ban on a religious procession.

Carrying placards, thumping their chests and chanting slogans, they marched some eight km (five miles) from the Jama Masjid mosque in the capital's old quarters to Parliament Street, some of them bloodied by self-inflicted wounds.
"Dissolve Uttar Pradesh government," read one banner.
The protesters shouted slogans against the chief minister of the northern state of Uttar Pradesh, Mayawati, and urged the federal government to release their leader.
They insisted on being arrested until then but police did not make any arrests.
"We also want to stay in jail as long as our leader is in jail," said Shabi Muhammad Kazmi, a local Moslem leader.

The demonstration followed the arrest on Sunday of Shi'ite leader Maulana Kalbe Jawwad in the northern city of Lucknow, which has a high proportion of Shi'ite Moslems and where the annual procession has been prohibited since 1977.
The ban was imposed in 1977 after 15 people were killed in clashes between members of the Shi'ite and Sunni sects.

The arrested Shi'ite leader led a drive against the ban on the annual procession which marks the death anniversary of the Prophet Mohammad's grandson, Hussain. He led a campaign which resulted in a procession on June 26.
Members of both the Sunni and the Shi'ite sects took part in Friday's procession claiming that Jawwad was not only the leader of the Shi'ite community but of the Moslem community as a whole.
This was the second demonstration by Moslems in a week against Jawwad's arrest.
Blood oozed from the bodies of the protesters as they hit themselves with "Matam-e-Hussaini," or steel whips tied with knives.
"From tomorrow, women and children will also submit themselves to voluntary arrest," Kazmi said.
